clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Case–control comparisons with permutation tests; examined sex differences and compared deviation distributions across groups; no clear association with symptom severity identified in provided materials.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Normative modeling of dynamic FC reveals more FEDN-MDD patients exhibit extreme deviations than controls, with notable differences in DMN, left ECN, and limbic networks; effects are more evident in males.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Most participants show few extreme deviations (<50 connectivities), but patients are overrepresented among those with many deviations (≥100 connectivities: 4.74% patients vs 3.35% controls). Network fluctuation characteristics are increased in patients; significant group differences concentrate in DMN, left ECN, and limbic networks, particularly among males. Excluding top 5% outliers reduces case–control differences, suggesting prior group effects may be driven by small subsets.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Normative modeling complements case–control analyses by characterizing individual-level heterogeneity. Findings suggest a subset of FEDN-MDD patients exhibit marked dynamic FC deviations, with potential utility for stratification and targeted analyses.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional normative modeling; incomplete reporting of QC procedures and software; unclear handling of site/scanner effects within the NM step; limited symptom measures hindered detection of symptom–deviation associations; sliding-window choices may influence dynamic FC results.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Dynamic FC estimated via sliding windows; inherent networks derived using GIG-ICA. Supplementary Table S1 lists multi-site scanner parameters. Methods reference Yan et al., PNAS 2019 for preprocessing details.
